crop.notes: Whole article, from the headline 'TOM ALLEN "BESTED." The Ex-Heavy-Weight Champion Sustains a Black Eye and Bruised Ear' to the closing rule, in column 1 of page 5.

ocr.notes: Readable and mostly right, but some words differ from the image: Dan was 'sitting' (not 'standing') before his door; 'that ain't right' (not 'fair'); Allen said 'Oh! what a puddin' I've got. This 'ere fellow thinks 'e's a fighter!' (OCR has 'nap'); 'fell like a log' (not 'rock'); 'four times in the face' (not 'twice'); Allen's 'Daly says he fought me' and 'you'd think a whole theater was out' (OCR 'got me', 'I think'); 'prompted Allen to make the fight' (not 'led ... attack').

title.suggested: Tom Allen "bested" in a street fight with the Daly brothers

summary.suggested: The St. Louis Post-Dispatch reported that Tom Allen was knocked down by Dan Daly in a 2 a.m. street fight at Seventh and Market streets; Allen said a crowd tripped and kicked him, and the case was continued in Police Court.

metadata.notes: Masthead reads 'St. Louis Post-Dispatch, Monday, June 18, 1888', page 5. The fight was 'yesterday morning about the hour of 2 o'clock', i.e. Sunday June 17, 1888.

facts.fact: Allen fought Dan Daly (middleweight champion of Missouri) in a street brawl near Seventh and Market streets, St. Louis; Daly's side said Allen was knocked down and begged him to quit, while Charley Daly chased Allen's friends 'Dutchy' Frank Neal and Steve Hearne
places: Seventh and Market streets, St. Louis

facts.fact: Allen said a crowd from Daly's place jumped on him, tripped him and kicked him, and that the matter was not over
facts.quote: About fifty of 'em came out and jumped on me. There was too many of 'em to hurt me. ... This thing, though, ain't over yet by a long shot.

facts.fact: Allen and Charley Daly were taken to the station and gave bond; the Police Court case was continued until Thursday at Allen's request
Allen was keeping a free-and-easy on Market Street, St. Louis

notes: The Dalys' place of business was on Seventh Street near Market, close to Allen's.
